r: The foolproof crêpe batter, thin and light, for a snack or Candlemas.
Put the flour, sugar and a pinch of salt in a mixing bowl, and make a well in the middle.
Add the eggs, then the milk a little at a time, whisking to avoid lumps.
Add the melted butter and leave to rest for 30 min if you can.|Rest|30
Cook the crêpes in a hot, lightly buttered pan, 1 min on each side.
Cow's milk is replaced by oat milk and the butter by oil.
Just as thin, with no dairy.
Mix the flour, sugar and salt, then add the eggs.
Pour in the oat milk a little at a time, whisking, then add the oil.
Cook the crêpes in a hot, oiled pan.
Buckwheat galettes with ham, egg and emmental
Buckwheat flour, with ham, egg and cheese.
The classic Breton galettes: ham, egg and emmental.
Mix the flour, 1 egg, a pinch of salt and 60 cl of cold water. Leave to rest for 1 h.|Rest|60
Cook a galette in a buttered pan for 2 min.|Pan|2
Flip it, add the emmental and ham, and crack an egg into the middle.
Fold the edges into a square and cook until the white is set.|Pan|3
Waffles that are crisp outside and soft inside.
Mix the flour, baking powder, sugars and salt.
Add the egg yolks, then the milk and melted butter.
Whisk the egg whites until stiff and fold them in gently.
Cook in the hot waffle iron for 3 to 4 min.|Waffle iron|4
A yeast dough with pearl sugar that caramelises.
Thick Belgian waffles with caramelised pearl sugar.
Dissolve the yeast in the warm milk.
Mix the flour, eggs, milk and salt, then work in the soft butter.
Leave to rise for 1 h somewhere warm.|Rising|60
Add the pearl sugar, shape into balls and cook them for 4 min in the waffle iron.|Waffle iron|4
Less butter, and fromage blanc in the batter.
Mix the flour, baking powder and sugar.
Add the eggs, fromage blanc, milk and melted butter.
Cook for 4 min in the hot waffle iron.|Waffle iron|4
Thick, fluffy pancakes to serve with maple syrup.
Mix the flour, baking powder, sugar and a pinch of salt.
Add the eggs, milk and melted butter, and mix just enough.
Pour a small ladle of batter into a hot buttered pan.
Flip when bubbles appear, after 2 min, and cook for 1 min on the other side.|Pan|3
A mashed banana replaces some of the sugar.
Mash the bananas and mix them with the eggs and milk.
Add the flour and baking powder.
Cook small pancakes for 2 min on each side in a buttered pan.|Pan|4
The flour is replaced by blitzed porridge oats.
Wholesome, filling pancakes with no added sugar.
Blitz the porridge oats with the banana, eggs, milk and baking powder.
Cook for 2 min on each side in a non-stick pan.|Pan|4
The no-waste dessert: stale bread soaked in sweet milk and eggs, then browned in butter.
Mix the milk, eggs, sugars and a little cinnamon.
Soak the slices of bread on both sides.
Brown them in the butter for 2 min on each side.|Pan|4
Sprinkle with a little sugar and serve hot.
Brioche replaces the bread, with a touch of caramel.
An even more indulgent version, with caramelised brioche.
Mix the milk, eggs and half the sugar.
Quickly dip the slices of brioche.
Brown them in the butter, sprinkle with the rest of the sugar and let it caramelise for 1 min on each side.|Pan|5
A savoury version with cheese and ham.
French toast as an evening meal, topped with melted cheese.
Beat the eggs with the milk, salt and pepper.
Soak the bread and brown it in the butter for 2 min on one side.|Pan|2
Flip it, add the ham and emmental, cover and cook for 3 min.|Pan|3
The cake that is gooey in the middle, everyone's favourite dessert.
Melt the chocolate and butter together.
Whisk the eggs with the sugar, then add the chocolate and flour.
Pour into a buttered tin and bake for 22 min: the centre should still wobble.|Oven|22
The butter is replaced by apple purée.
The gooey cake, in a lighter version.
Melt the chocolate and mix it with the apple purée.
Add the eggs beaten with the sugar, then the flour.
The flour is replaced by ground almonds.
A gooey chocolate and almond cake, gluten-free.
Whisk the eggs with the sugar, add the chocolate, then the ground almonds.
A dense, fudgy brownie with crunchy walnuts.
Whisk the eggs with the sugar, then add the chocolate, flour, a pinch of salt and the chopped walnuts.
Pour into a square tin and bake for 20 min.|Oven|20
Leave to cool before cutting into squares.
Banana replaces some of the butter and sugar.
A soft, no-waste brownie made with very ripe bananas.
Melt the chocolate with the butter.
Mash the bananas and mix with the eggs, sugar, chocolate and flour.
The flour is replaced by ground almonds.
Add the eggs beaten with the sugar, the ground almonds and the chopped hazelnuts.
Cookies that are crisp at the edges and soft in the middle.
Mix the soft butter and sugar, then add the egg.
Add the flour, baking powder, a pinch of salt and the chocolate chips.
Shape into balls and place them well apart on a baking tray.
Bake for 10 min: they should stay soft in the middle.|Oven|10
Porridge oats and raisins replace some of the flour.
Rustic cookies with oats and raisins.
Mix the butter and sugar, then add the egg.
Add the flour, oats, cinnamon and raisins.
Drop small heaps onto a baking tray and bake for 12 min.|Oven|12
Cocoa in the dough and white chocolate chunks.
Cocoa cookies with melting white chocolate.
Mix the butter and sugar, then the egg.
Add the flour, cocoa, baking powder and the white chocolate in pieces.
Shape into balls and bake for 10 min.|Oven|10
Well-risen, soft muffins full of blueberries.
Mix the flour, sugar and baking powder in one bowl, and the eggs, milk and butter in another.
Pour the liquid onto the flour and barely mix, then add the blueberries.
Fill muffin cases three-quarters full and bake for 20 min.|Oven|20
Cocoa and chocolate chips replace the blueberries.
All-chocolate muffins, just like from the bakery.
Mix the dry ingredients, then the liquids separately.
Combine the two without overmixing, and add the chocolate chips.
Fill the cases and bake for 20 min.|Oven|20
A savoury version, for party snacks or the lunch box.
Savoury muffins with courgette and feta.
Preheat the oven to 190 °C. Grate the courgette and squeeze out the water.
Mix the flour, baking powder, salt and pepper, then the eggs, milk and oil.
Add the courgette and the diced feta.
Fill the cases and bake for 22 min.|Oven|22
A moist, fragrant cake topped with a lemon glaze.
Whisk the eggs and sugar, then add the melted butter and the zest and juice of one lemon.
Add the flour and baking powder, and pour into a loaf tin.
Mix the icing sugar with the juice of the other lemon and pour over the cooled cake.
The lemon cake, with poppy seeds.
Mix the eggs and sugar, then the butter, and the zest and juice of the lemons.
Add the flour, baking powder and poppy seeds.
Bake for 40 min in a loaf tin.|Oven|40
The butter is replaced by yogurt.
The lemon cake, soft and lighter.
Mix the eggs, sugar, yogurt, oil, and the zest and juice of the lemons.
Add the flour and baking powder.
The first cake everyone learns, soft and foolproof.
Pour the yogurt into a mixing bowl.
Add the eggs, sugar, flour, baking powder, vanilla sugar and oil, mixing as you go.
Pour into a buttered tin and bake for 35 min.|Oven|35
Thin slices of apple are added to the batter.
The yogurt cake, with soft apples.
Add the peeled apples in small pieces.
Half the batter is flavoured with cocoa.
The yogurt cake, marbled with chocolate.
Make the yogurt cake batter and divide it in two.
Add the cocoa to one half.
Pour the two batters into a tin, alternating them, and bake for 35 min.|Oven|35
